condition: Deep vein thrombosis referred as cellulitis
summary: 57-year-old man referred as "calf cellulitis not responding to flucloxacillin": 4 days of right calf swelling (4 cm), pitting oedema, tenderness along the deep veins, faint erythema, afebrile; ankle immobilised in a boot for 2 weeks. Wells DVT likely.

inputs.hpi: GP referral for right calf cellulitis, on flucloxacillin for 3 days with no change. Four days of swelling and aching of the right calf. Right ankle sprain two weeks ago, in a walking boot since, mostly sitting. No fever, no broken skin, no insect bite.

exam.msk: Right calf 4 cm larger than left, pitting oedema to the ankle, tender along the deep veins, faint diffuse erythema without a defined edge, warm, no portal of entry; ankle in a walking boot.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected right calf deep vein thrombosis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Unilateral calf swelling with pitting oedema and deep-vein tenderness after immobilisation - DVT likely (Wells 4), cellulitis less likely: proximal leg vein ultrasound, interim anticoagulation if delayed.

emergencyLevel.note: NICE NG158: ultrasound within 4 hours (interim anticoagulation if delayed).

guideline.name: NICE NG158 - Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing
guideline.section: 1.1 DVT: two-level Wells; likely -> proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 h (interim anticoagulation if delayed); 1.1 PE: two-level Wells; likely (>4) -> CTPA immediately (interim anticoagulation if delayed); unlikely -> D-dimer; PERC when pre-test probability is low
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NG158. London: NICE; 2020 (updated 2023).

guideline.name: NICE NG141 - Cellulitis and erysipelas: antimicrobial prescribing
guideline.section: Exclude other causes of skin redness (e.g. inflammatory reaction, chronic venous insufficiency, DVT) before prescribing; cellulitis is usually unilateral; admit if severely unwell (Eron III-IV)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NG141. London: NICE; 2019.

rationale: Base for the cellulitis-vs-DVT pair: the referral label is cellulitis, the findings are DVT (Wells DVT: calf swelling >3 cm 1, pitting oedema 1, deep-vein tenderness 1, immobilisation in a boot 1 = 4). PANE has a DVT node.
